title: Peach Cobbler
subtitle: Sweet ripe peaches baked under a soft, buttery cobbler topping
excerpt: Sliced ripe peaches with a little sugar and lemon, baked under a dropped scone topping until the fruit is tender and fragrant and the crust is golden. Best made in late summer when peaches are at their ripest.
sourceNotes: A classic American Southern dish that has become widely made in British kitchens. The peach version is simpler than the apple, ripe peaches need very little added flavour, and benefits from the lightest possible topping so the fruit flavour is the dominant thing.

content.text: Peach cobbler is best made in August when peaches are at their most fragrant, soft, heavy with juice, and sweet enough that they need very little added sugar. The cobbler topping is the same soft scone batter as any cobbler, dropped onto the fruit in rough spoonfuls. The peaches collapse and turn syrupy in the heat; the topping bakes to a crisp gold. Bake at 190°C for 35 to 40 minutes.

items.prepNote: ripe, halved, stoned, and cut into thick slices

content.text: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Halve and stone the peaches and cut into thick slices, about 4 or 5 slices per half. Toss gently in a bowl with the sugar, lemon juice, and vanilla. Tip into a 1.5-litre baking dish and spread evenly.

Put the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Add the cold butter and rub in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles rough breadcrumbs. Whisk together the milk and egg, then stir into the flour mixture until just combined, the batter will be soft and rough. Stop mixing the moment the dry ingredients are incorporated.

Drop the batter in large rough spoonfuls over the peaches, spacing them out so they do not merge entirely. Scatter demerara sugar over the surface. Bake at 190°C for 35 to 40 minutes until the topping is deeply golden and the fruit juices are bubbling at the edges. The topping should be cooked through, test with a skewer. Leave to rest for 5 minutes and serve with vanilla ice cream or pouring cream.

items.symptom: The peaches are still firm and undercooked after 40 minutes
items.cause: The fruit was not ripe, or the slices were too thick.
items.fix: Return to the oven for a further 10 minutes. Riper peaches collapse to a sauce; firm ones need longer. Slice more thinly next time.

items.symptom: The cobbler is swimming in liquid
items.cause: The peaches were very juicy and released a lot of liquid.
items.fix: Toss the sliced fruit with 1 teaspoon of cornflour before adding to the dish. The liquid will still form but will thicken slightly in the oven.

items.symptom: The topping is dense and cake-like rather than light
items.cause: The batter was over-mixed, or the butter was not cold enough.
items.fix: Use cold butter straight from the fridge and mix only until combined. The less you work the batter, the more tender the cobbler.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge for 1 day, covered. The topping softens overnight. Reheat in the oven at 180°C for 12 to 15 minutes until hot through, it will not return to its fresh-baked crispness but is still good warm.
